paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God cares about the health of His church, and love sometimes means taking sin seriously. The Corinthians were proud while a man among them had his father's wife (1 Corinthians 5:1-2). Paul says they should have been stricken with grief instead. Pride and grief can't share the same oven, baker.

Now look at WHY Paul says to act. The goal is that the man's spirit "may be saved on the Day of the Lord" (1 Corinthians 5:5). He also says "a little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (1 Corinthians 5:6). I've baked enough to know it, friend: you can't pick one bad ingredient out after it's mixed in. And Paul reminds them that they are a new batch, because "Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed" (1 Corinthians 5:7).

Paul also draws a clear line about who he means. He isn't talking about the people of this world, since then they "would have to leave this world" (1 Corinthians 5:10). He means anyone who claims to be a brother but lives that way, and God will judge those outside (1 Corinthians 5:11, 13). So here's what I take home, baker: ask what's rising in your own dough first, and keep your church's life honest, sincere and true (1 Corinthians 5:8).
